Solutions · Modular Data Centers

Fabricate the facility where the work is controlled.

Evolve builds data-center modules in its own shop and connects them to the site, the power and the commissioning plan.

Discuss a Modular ProjectCompare Delivery Approaches

The situation

Owners choose modular delivery to move defined scope out of the field, run fabrication and site work in parallel and add capacity in phases. The decision only pays off when the module boundaries, the site interfaces and the acceptance plan are designed together.

What Evolve delivers

Evolve provides self-performed modular fabrication. Modular systems can be factory-built and site-set in days, depending on the project and the project plan. Evolve also supports the surrounding work: planning, design, procurement, site construction, power, commissioning, monitoring and maintenance.

How the lifecycle applies

  1. 01

    Plan

    Define the operational requirement, the module scope, the site interfaces and the transportation assumptions.

    Explore
  2. 02

    Design

    Coordinate the module with the building, site, power and controls, and freeze only what has been resolved.

    Explore
  3. 03

    Build

    Advance fabrication while the site is prepared, then set, connect and commission the modules.

    Explore
  4. 04

    Power

    Align generation and critical-power decisions with the module and site design.

    Explore
  5. 05

    Maintain

    Carry equipment information and access needs into monitoring and maintenance planning.

    Explore

Experience at a glance

Evolve has completed more than 2,200 mission-critical projects and deployed more than 5,300 MW of power. Project-specific customer and facility histories remain confidential.

Direct answers

Does Evolve fabricate its own modules?

Yes. Evolve provides self-performed modular fabrication, and the final scope and delivery sequence are established for each project.

Is modular always faster?

No universal schedule should be assumed. Design maturity, procurement, logistics, site readiness and commissioning still control the outcome.

What should be decided before choosing modular delivery?

The module boundaries, the site interfaces, the design-freeze timing, the transport and setting requirements and the acceptance process.
